tests.procedure: Under strong white light check each received sample container separately in a clean transparent watch glass for foreign particles, colour and conformity with the visual specification.

details.bpStmText: White or almost white powder or granules.

tests.procedure: Weigh 100 mg in a stoppered tube; add 0.1 mL solvent, shake 1 min, hold at 25.0 ± 0.5 °C for 15 min, repeat shake/hold once if not dissolved; add 0.9 mL, then 2 mL, then 7 mL solvent with the same shake and hold steps to classify very soluble / freely soluble / soluble / sparingly soluble; if still undissolved use 10 mg in 10 mL (slightly soluble), then 1 mg in 10 mL (very slightly soluble), else practically insoluble. Repeat with ethanol (96 per cent).

details.reference: BP 2024 (SC IV K.) Characters Section in Monographs

tests.procedure: UV identification: test solution 50.0 mg in water to 250.0 mL; dilute 2.0 mL to 200.0 mL with 0.1 M hydrochloric acid. Spectral range 230-350 nm; read the specific absorbance at the absorption maximum (264 nm).
IR identification: examine the spectrum obtained for the sample and compare it with the spectrum obtained from Potassium sorbate RS.

Thermal decomposition identification: dissolve 1.0 g in 50 mL water; add 10 mL dilute hydrochloric acid and shake; filter the crystalline precipitate; wash with water; dry in vacuo over sulfuric acid for 4 h; determine the melting point of the residue with a calibrated melting point apparatus.

details.dilutedHydrochloricAcid: 10 mL (hydrochloric acid, dilute: 20 g HCl to 100 mL with water)
details.drying: in vacuo over sulfuric acid, 4 h

tests.procedure: Reaction of potassium: dissolve 0.2 g in 2 mL water; add 2 mL dilute acetic acid; filter; add 1 mL of freshly prepared 100 g/L sodium cobaltinitrite solution; a yellow or orange-yellow precipitate forms immediately.

details.diluteAceticAcid: 2 mL (acetic acid, dilute: 12 g glacial acetic acid to 100 mL with water)
details.reagent: sodium cobaltinitrite 100 g/L, freshly prepared, 1 mL

tests.procedure: Appearance of solution: put 10 mL of solution S and the same volume of reference solution Y5 in two identical Nessler tubes and compare; solution S must be clear and not more intensely coloured than reference solution Y5.

details.solutionS: 2.5 g in CO2-free water to 50 mL
details.referenceSolutionY5: 12.5 mL standard solution Y + 87.5 mL hydrochloric acid (10 g/L)

tests.procedure: Acidity or alkalinity: to 20 mL solution S add 0.1 mL phenolphthalein solution; titrate with 0.1 M sodium hydroxide or 0.1 M hydrochloric acid to the colour change; record the volume used (NMT 0.25 mL).

details.solutionS: 2.5 g in CO2-free water to 50 mL

tests.procedure: Aldehydes (limit test): sample = 1.0 g in 30 mL water and 50 mL 2-propanol, adjust to pH 4 with 1 M hydrochloric acid, dilute to 100 mL with water; to 10 mL add 1 mL decolorized fuchsin solution and stand 30 min. Standard = 1.5 mL acetaldehyde standard solution (100 ppm) + 1 mL decolorized fuchsin solution + 4 mL 2-propanol + 4.5 mL water, diluted to 100 mL with water, stand 30 min. Sample colour must not be more intense than the standard.

details.limit: maximum 0.15 per cent, expressed as acetaldehyde
details.reference: BP Appendix V L cited in STM (see openQuestions)

tests.procedure: Weigh a previously dried and cooled weighing bottle (W0), add 1.000 g sample (W1 = bottle + material); dry in calibrated oven at 105 °C for 3 h, cool in desiccator, weigh (W2); repeat drying to constant weight. % loss on drying = (W1 - W2) / (W1 - W0) x 100.

Assay (titration): dissolve 0.120 g sample in 20 mL anhydrous acetic acid; titrate with 0.1 M perchloric acid using 0.1 mL crystal violet solution as indicator until the colour changes from violet to bluish green. 1 mL of 0.1 M perchloric acid = 15.02 mg potassium sorbate. Assay = (E.P x eq.wt x F x 100 * 100) / Wt x (100 - LOD), dried substance.

details.titrantStandardization: 0.170 g potassium hydrogen phthalate in 50 mL anhydrous acetic acid, titrated potentiometrically; M = (weight of C8H5KO4 x 1000) / (204.2 x E.P)
details.titrantPreparation: 8.5 mL perchloric acid in about 900 mL glacial acetic acid, add 30 mL acetic anhydride, dilute to 1000.0 mL with glacial acetic acid, stand 24 h
details.equivalenceFactor: 1 mL of 0.1 M perchloric acid = 15.02 mg potassium sorbate
details.formula: (E.P x eq.wt x F x 100 * 100) / Wt x (100 - LOD); E.P = titre (mL), F = titrant factor, Wt = sample weight (g), LOD from loss on drying

openQuestions.question: Assay formula: 'eq.wt' is defined as 'Equivalent Weight of Citric Acid' (apparently a copy error for potassium sorbate), and the factor reads '100 * 100' inside the bracket; formula loaded as written, confirm.
Aldehydes limit test cites 'BP Appendix V L. Determination of pH Values' as its reference; the reference is not confirmed for this test.
Micro methods (TAMC, TYMC, E. coli) are not described in this STM; the rows are loaded from the spec sheet limits only.
